request.text: a robot that learns to play music

pitch.hero: Pip, a small repair-shop robot with a dented tin chest
pitch.want: To learn to play the old piano so it can make a tune like the ones it hears through the wall
pitch.obstacle: Its metal fingers are too heavy and clunky, and every key it presses lands with a loud thud
pitch.stake: The shop will be sold and the piano taken away before Pip ever plays a whole song

pip.name: Pip
pip.role: small repair-shop robot with a dented tin chest
pip.want: To play the old piano and make a tune like the ones through the wall

explorer.name: Explorer
explorer.role: curious young helper who guides Pip, addressed as you
explorer.want: To help Pip play a whole song before the shop sells

wren.name: Mrs. Wren
wren.role: neighbor who plays piano next door
wren.want: To share her music with someone who listens

truth.statement: The tune through the wall is Mrs. Wren playing her piano next door. Pip learns that soft felt pads on its fingers stop the thuds, and plays a whole song on the old piano before it leaves.
truth.question: Where does the tune come from, and how can Pip play it?

f1.text: Pip longs to play a tune like the ones it hears through the wall.

f2.text: Pip's metal fingers are heavy and every key it presses lands with a thud.

f3.text: The repair shop will be sold soon and the old piano taken away.

f4.text: The shop floor has many doors and corners Pip could try.

f5.text: Pip looks over the workbench of spare parts.

f6.text: A jar of loose springs sits on the bench.

f7.text: Pip bounces a spring on a key and it twangs oddly.

f8.text: Pip finds a coil that is too bouncy to press keys with.

f9.text: Pip tries a rubber washer on a finger but it slips off.

f10.text: Pip tries tapping with a wooden spoon and it clacks.

f11.text: Pip decides the piano is too hard and gives up for today.

f12.text: A shelf of soft scraps and cloths stands by the window.

f13.text: Pip finds a scrap of velvet on the shelf.

f14.text: The velvet is too thin and bunches up on Pip's finger.

f15.text: Pip finds a thick wool sock on the shelf.

f16.text: The sock is too bulky to fit between the keys.

f17.text: Pip gathers soft scraps to bring to the piano.

f18.text: A scrap of piano felt lies under the shelf.

f19.text: Pip holds the felt scrap and feels how quiet it is.

f20.text: Pip hides the scraps in a drawer and forgets them for now.

f21.text: The back room is dusty and full of boxes.

f22.text: Pip finds a box labeled old piano parts.

f23.text: Pip finds a small hammer with a soft head inside the box.

f24.text: Pip learns a piano hammer is padded with felt.

f25.text: Pip sees a dusty photo of a smiling piano player.

f26.text: Pip reads a note saying the piano was loved once.

f27.text: Pip wonders who played the piano long ago.

f28.text: Pip presses an ear to the wall to listen.

f29.text: Faint notes come through the wall in a slow pattern.

f30.text: Pip hums the pattern back to itself.

f31.text: Pip notices the notes are played gently, not hit.

f32.text: Pip hears the tune stop and start again like a song.

f33.text: Pip knocks on the wall too hard and the music stops, so Pip leaves.

f34.text: A pile of sheet music sits on the piano lid.

f35.text: Pip cannot read the dots on the page yet.

f36.text: Pip spots a short song with only five notes.

f37.text: Pip counts the five notes on the page.

f38.text: The notes match the first part of the tune Pip hears.

f39.text: Pip learns the song is called Little Lantern.

f40.text: Pip finds a note on the sheet music written by Mrs. Wren.

f41.text: A tuning fork lies near the piano.

f42.text: Pip taps the fork and hears a clear single tone.

f43.text: Pip learns tapping lightly gives a clear tone.

f44.text: Pip finds the piano is a little out of tune.

f45.text: Pip turns a tuning pin with a careful wrench.

f46.text: Pip loosens a key by accident and it sticks.

f47.text: Pip fixes the sticky key with oil.

f48.text: Pip tries to rush the tuning and a string twangs sourly.

f49.text: Pip finds a small door in the piano's side holding a music box.

f50.text: The tune through the wall is Mrs. Wren playing her own piano next door.

f51.text: Pip pauses to think about what it has learned.

f52.text: Pip plays a few clumsy notes with Mrs. Wren's help in mind.

f53.text: Pip wonders if softness is the answer.

f54.text: Soft felt pads on Pip's fingers stop the thuds and make gentle notes.

f55.text: Pip plays a whole song on the old piano.

f56.text: Pip walks away from the piano and does not play today.

f57.text: Pip plays the song for the shopkeeper.

f58.text: Pip hears applause from next door.

f59.text: Pip plays with Mrs. Wren at the wall.

f60.text: Pip takes the song to Mrs. Wren's door.

f61.text: Pip plays alone at night in the quiet shop.

f62.text: Pip teaches the shopkeeper a few notes.

f63.text: The shopkeeper decides to keep the piano.

f64.text: Mrs. Wren offers to buy the shop's piano and keep it nearby.

f65.text: Pip plays Little Lantern to the street.

f66.text: The shop is saved and Pip plays at home.

f67.text: The piano moves next door and Pip visits it often.

f68.text: Pip plays beside the shopkeeper at home.

f69.text: Pip and Mrs. Wren play together by the wall.

f70.text: Pip plays the song to the whole street.

f71.text: Pip falls asleep happy beside the piano.
